Let
\[
S=\sum_{n=0}^\infty \frac{\cos n\theta}{2^n}.
\]
Using the standard geometric series formula,
\[
\sum_{n=0}^\infty r^n\cos(n\theta)=\frac{1-r\cos\theta}{1-2r\cos\theta+r^2},
\qquad |r|<1.
\]
Here \(r=\frac12\) and \(\cos\theta=\frac15\). Substituting,
\[
S=\frac{1-\frac12\cdot \frac15}{1-2\cdot \frac12\cdot \frac15+\left(\frac12\right)^2}.
\]
Simplify:
\[
S=\frac{1-\frac1{10}}{1-\frac15+\frac14}
=\frac{\frac9{10}}{\frac{21}{20}}
=\frac9{10}\cdot \frac{20}{21}
=\frac{18}{21}
=\frac67.
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{\frac67}\).
